differences.what: massing: the draft's 5.5 m box under a generic shaped gable is now the photograph's narrow party-wall front, 7.56 m across between the north corner and the party line with 2011, three tiers of lights over a raised stone basement, its side walls stopping at the kneelers (11.95 m)

the ogee gable: the front carried up past the side walls into a concave-sided spire to its crest at about 16.4 m, its outline laid over the print within about 0.1-0.2 m at every height; its attic pair under the apex

the gable's south foot: the print's outline runs on down past the kneeler to about 10.3 m over the party wall, where the build leaves the front's width at the kneelers (11.97 m) on both sides and the hip's eave shows over the party wall
the street lights: the ground floor's window (two lights on a mullion under a transom) under the oriel, the small light beside it, the third storey's paired light, each on the print's place and size
the ground window's head about 0.15 m under the print's (it clears the oriel's corbel)
the oriel: three lights from the second floor on a corbelled apron under the string course, on the print's lights

the oriel's lights: each 0.75 m clear in a 1.0 m frame where the print's are about 0.9-1.1 m between mullions, and the oriel a flat front on short cants where the print's is slightly bowed (both about 0.2 m)

the oriel's carved frieze over its lights: a band of carved rings round the oriel under its cap, 8.45-9.2 m, where the print's carved frieze runs from about 8.3 to 8.9 m under a moulded cap to 9.2 m (T-1914)
the oriel's frieze band about 0.15 m higher than the print's, and its carving drawn as a run of rings where the print's is foliage in three large cartouches
the oriel's carved apron under its lights (5.05-5.9 m): the build's corbel courses are plain stone
the street lights' stone surrounds of long and short blocks, round the ground window, the small light and the paired light
the low coped stone wall on the street line, about 0.47 m high, from about 0.6 m along the lot to short of the walk to the stoop

the door: one dark leaf under a two-light fanlight on a transom bar (3.8 m) in an elliptical head (crown 4.3 m, 1.08 m across), a moulded stone ring round the head and down the jambs, and a stone pilaster each side under a capital, on the print's place and size (T-1914)
the fanlight's Y-tracery drawn as a plain mullion between its two lights, and the moulded ring narrower than the print's deep reveal
the door's pilasters stop under their capitals at about 4.5 m where the print carries them up through the carved panels to pinnacles at about 5.6 m, a third pinnacle over the arch's crown
the carved panels over the door: a carved course of rings from 4.8 to 5.3 m over the door between its pilasters, on the print's place (T-1914)

the carved panels over the door: laid as a carved stone panel over the door's run alone (4.65-5.25 m, s 5.4-7.2 m, its foot on the pilasters' capitals), the brick running on beside it as the print's does, where K01 had laid a 0.5 m course across the whole front (T-3365)
the print's thin course at about 5.25 m running from the oriel to the party wall over the carving: not laid (about 0.1 m deep)

the windows' moulded hoods (the ground window's hood on consoles, the paired light's hood rising to the pendant, the small light's hood block), and the carved pendant in the gable: under the build's plain lintels (T-1914)

the north corner: the print, read at 2x with its contrast stretched, shows brick up the corner to the string course and a pale stone strip about 0.5 m across from the string course to the kneeler (9.2-11.75 m), not quoins from grade; laid as stone courses up the corner from 9.2 m to the wall head, returned 0.3 m on the flank (T-3365)
the gable's crest: a carved block on the apex in the print, a turned finial in the build (T-1914)

the basement's three square lights under the ground window: cut in the rusticated base at the print's centres (1.96, 3.02, 4.05 m), 0.74 m across, from 0.08 m to the base's top at 0.85 m, 0.08 m under the print's heads (T-3365)

the base's top: the print's rock-faced stone runs on over the lights to about 1.35 m under a smooth band to about 1.85 m, where the build's smooth coping is 0.85-1.25 m (about 0.4-0.5 m low, the T-1913 reading of the base, unchanged here)
the string course across the front at about 9.1 m and the stone sill course at the principal floor
the stoop: a straight flight between stone cheek walls from the walk to the door at the south end, on the print's place and width
the near tall stack on the north flank: about 0.6 m south of the print's place (K01 stands it inside the main body) and its corbelled cap plain
the north flank: its projection's front face and the tall light near the front corner, seen edge-on; the print's flank is mostly hidden by the parkway tree
the far stack and the cornice at the print's left edge: north of this lot through the camera, read as 2005's
the two bare parkway trees: not this record's (the street's trees)
colour: the print is monochrome; the brick is the register's rough red-brown and the basement its brownstone

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
